title: The Iliad: Patroclus Changes Everything
subtitle: Borrowed armour, a friend's death, and rage redirected

narrativeBlocks.title: The compromise
narrativeBlocks.body: The battle reaches the ships — the exact point Achilles said he would fight. But he still will not yield his pride: instead Patroclus begs to borrow his armour so the Trojans, thinking Achilles returned, will panic. Achilles agrees — with a warning: drive them off, then come back. Do not chase glory to the walls.

narrativeBlocks.title: The disguise works — then fails
narrativeBlocks.body: The Trojans see the armour and break. But Patroclus, drunk on his own rampage, ignores the warning and presses toward Troy itself — where Apollo strikes him from behind, and Hector finishes him.

narrativeBlocks.title: The news
narrativeBlocks.body: 'Patroclus has fallen, and a fight is raging about his naked body.' Achilles's grief is volcanic — he pours dust over his head, and the sound of his crying reaches Thetis under the sea.

narrativeBlocks.title: Rage finds its true target
narrativeBlocks.body: The quarrel with Agamemnon now means nothing to him. He reconciles instantly — the gifts, Briseis, all irrelevant. His rage has a new name: Hector. He will return to battle knowing his own death follows, because the Fates have already promised it.

narrativeBlocks.title: The price of pride
narrativeBlocks.body: Every death at Troy traces back to that first quarrel — but Patroclus's death is the one Achilles caused himself, by staying out and letting another man wear his armour.

quiz.explanation: Patroclus goes beyond his mission — chasing to Troy's walls, Apollo strikes him, Hector kills him. His death turns Achilles's rage from Agamemnon to Hector.
